Predicting from a network regression

Source: R/model_predict.R
predict.Rd

predict() gives the predicted value of the outcome for each dyad.

  • For a netreg, from estimate_mrqap(), it predicts either the dyads that the model was fitted on, or the dyads of newdata.

  • For a netlm or netlogit, from net_regression() in {migraph} before 2.0.0, it predicts the rows of a design matrix.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'netreg'
predict(object, newdata = NULL, type = c("link", "response"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'netlm'
predict(object, newdata = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netlogit'
predict(object, newdata = NULL, type = c("link", "response"), ...)

Arguments

object

A netreg object, as returned by estimate_mrqap(), or a netlm or netlogit object.

newdata

The dyads to predict. For a netreg, NULL (the default) predicts the dyads that the model was fitted on. Otherwise, a data frame or a matrix with a column for each predictor, named as the coefficients are, e.g. ego_Citations. A column for an interaction, e.g. ego_Age:same_Grp, is computed from its parts where it is absent. The model's own dyad-level data, object$pred, has these columns. A matrix without column names needs a column for each coefficient, in their order, with the intercept first. For a netlm or netlogit, a design matrix with the same columns as the fitted model.

type

The scale of the predictions: "link" (the default), the scale of the linear predictor, or "response", the scale of the outcome, e.g. probabilities for a binomial model and expected counts for a count model. For a gaussian model the two are the same.

...

Not used.

Value

A numeric vector of predicted values, one for each dyad or row.

Details

Without newdata, the prediction for a netreg is the fitted value of each dyad of the model, with any random intercepts and absorbed fixed effects.

With newdata, the prediction comes from the coefficients only. A random intercept is then zero, as for a dyad of a node the model has not seen. A fixed effect is absorbed, so it has no coefficient, and a model with fixed effects predicts only the dyads it was fitted on. For a zero-inflated Poisson model, the zero-inflation part reads the same columns as the count part.

Examples

networkers <- manynet::ison_networkers |>
  manynet::to_subgraph(Discipline == "Sociology")
model1 <- estimate_mrqap(weight ~ ego(Citations) + alter(Citations),
                         networkers, times = 5)
# The fitted value of each dyad
head(predict(model1))
#> [1] 20.209569 13.467296 23.382403  7.914836 11.087671 22.589195
# A sender with 10 citations, to a receiver with 50
predict(model1, data.frame(ego_Citations = 10, alter_Citations = 50))
#> [1] 16.4984
